evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. A guest reboot changes both the manager PID and the service invocation ID, so it can satisfy manager_restarted without any actual manager restart, while the separate boot_id_changed check compares only the reboot phase's own before/after boot IDs and cannot rule this out. Requiring the same nonempty boot ID on both sides of the manager snapshot binds the check to its stated meaning (a manager restart within one boot) and is a small correctness repair, not a new protection requirement. The reboot snapshots already show boot_id is captured by this snapshot mechanism; if the manager before/after snapshots do not include it, capturing it is part of the same fix.
